findings_qualitative.value: Brightest sources are dust dominated; weaker ones show free-free contamination

evidence.quote: The brightest sources are dominated by (partially optically thick) dust emission, while there is an important degree of contamination from ionized gas free-free emission in weaker sources.

findings_qualitative.value: Lack of low-mass dense cores relative to Salpeter IMF

evidence.quote: There seems to be a lack of low-mass dense cores in both regions.

claims.hypothesis: Is the 1.3 mm emission of the sources dust or ionized gas?
claims.experiment: Spectral indices across band 6 and comparison with VLA 40 GHz and SMA 345 GHz
claims.result: Bright sources have alpha 2-4; some faint sources have flat/negative alpha coincident with VLA HII regions
claims.finding: Dust dominates bright sources; free-free contaminates weaker ones

evidence.quote: This analysis confirms a degree of contamination from free-free emission in the Sgr B2 clouds even at wavelengths as long as 1 mm

claims.hypothesis: How is mass distributed in the two regions?
claims.experiment: Masses from 242 GHz fluxes at 50 and 100 K
claims.result: AN01 holds ~73% of N mass; AM01+AM02 only ~50% of M mass
claims.finding: Sgr B2(N) is dominated by a single object, Sgr B2(M) is fragmented

evidence.quote: Differently, Sgr B2(M) appears more fragmented with the two most massive cores (sources AM01 and AM02) accounting only for 50% (about 3000 $M_\odot$) of the total mass.

claims.hypothesis: Does chemical richness correlate with core mass?
claims.experiment: Lines per GHz and line luminosity fraction versus N(H2) and mass, linear fits
claims.result: Positive trends for cores not associated with ionized gas
claims.finding: More massive cores are more chemically rich, possibly a sensitivity effect

evidence.loc: 4.3 Chemical content in the continuum sources
evidence.quote: There are hints of a correlation where the most massive and dense cores are associated with the most chemically-rich sources.

evidence.quote: In order to determine the continuum emission in these line-rich sources, we use a new statistical method, STATCONT
